prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: hit while turning left in Katy, Texas. Injury: neck and back strain. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1488; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not have my name in a transcript for a test file, but you can use the placeholder in the caption.
Q: Understood. Let's proceed with the accident. Where were you driving when the collision happened?
A: I was in Katy, Texas, on a city road near a shopping center. I was turning left into the center's entrance.
Q: What time of day was it, and what were the weather and road conditions?
A: It was in the afternoon. The sky was clear and the pavement was dry. Traffic was moderate.
Q: Describe how the collision occurred.
A: I had the green light and was waiting for a gap in oncoming traffic. When it looked clear, I started my turn. The other vehicle came through the intersection and struck the front passenger side of my car.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before you began the turn?
A: I checked both directions. I didn't see it until it was close, and I had very little time to react.
Q: Did you lose consciousness or hit your head?
A: No. I was shaken, but I stayed awake and didn't strike my head on anything.
Q: What injuries did you notice immediately after the collision?
A: My neck felt stiff and sore right away, and my lower back ached. I didn't think it was serious at first.
Q: When did you first seek medical care?
A: I went to an urgent care clinic later that same day because the pain got worse overnight. They diagnosed a neck and back strain and gave me medication and instructions to rest.
Q: Who has treated you since then?
A: I've seen my primary care physician and a physical therapist. I've been doing exercises at home as well.
Q: How often are you attending physical therapy?
A: About twice a week for the first several weeks, and now I'm going less often as things improve.
Q: How have your daily activities been affected?
A: Simple things are harder. I have trouble lifting groceries, sitting through long periods at my desk, and I can't do my weekend yard work the way I used to.
Q: Have you missed any work because of your injuries?
A: I took a few days off in the first week and worked modified hours for a while afterward.
Q: Before this accident, had you ever had neck or back problems?
A: No, not that required treatment. I had occasional stiffness after long workdays, but nothing like this.
Q: Are you currently still experiencing pain?
A: Yes, especially in the mornings and after I've been sitting or driving for a while.
